cities.name: Chandigarh
cities.overview: India's first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier in the 1950s, and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana.
cities.history: Planned after Partition as the new capital of Indian Punjab, with Le Corbusier as chief architect in the 1950s. It's now shared by Punjab and Haryana.

places.name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
places.shortDescription: A whimsical sculpture garden built in secret by Nek Chand from broken tiles, bangles and industrial waste.
places.description: The Rock Garden is a maze of courtyards, waterfalls, arches and narrow passages populated by thousands of figures of people and animals, all made from recycled materials such as broken crockery, bangles, electrical fittings and rubble. Paths lead through themed sections that reveal new scenes at every turn. It is a joy for children and adults alike. Allow at least an hour.
places.history: Nek Chand, a road inspector, began building the garden secretly on government land around 1957. When it was discovered in 1975, the authorities chose to protect it, and it opened to the public in 1976.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; avoid the heat of May–June.

entryFee.note: Small entry fee for adults and children.

places.name: Sukhna Lake
places.shortDescription: A reservoir at the foot of the Shivalik hills where Chandigarh comes to walk, jog and go boating.
places.description: Sukhna Lake stretches along the city's northern edge with the Shivalik hills behind it. A long promenade along the dam is popular for morning walks and sunset strolls, and pedal boats and rowing boats can be hired. Migratory birds visit in winter. The lake is a short walk from the Rock Garden, so the two pair easily.
places.history: The lake was created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe, a seasonal stream from the Shivaliks, as part of Le Corbusier's plan for the city.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March; early mornings and sunsets are loveliest.

places.name: Capitol Complex
places.shortDescription: Le Corbusier's UNESCO-listed government complex, with the Open Hand Monument at its heart.
places.description: The Capitol Complex brings together three monumental concrete buildings by Le Corbusier: the Secretariat, the Legislative Assembly and the High Court, linked by a vast esplanade with the Open Hand Monument, symbol of the city, and the Tower of Shadows. The buildings are still in use, so visits are by guided tour that must be booked in advance with photo ID. Fans of modern architecture should not miss it.
places.history: The complex was designed by Le Corbusier and built from the early 1950s. It was inscribed in 2016 as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier', which spans seven countries.

entryFee.note: Free guided tours; book ahead and carry photo ID.

timings.hours: Guided tours on working days, usually 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM

sources.title: The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier – UNESCO

places.name: Zakir Hussain Rose Garden
places.shortDescription: Asia's largest rose garden, with 50,000 bushes over 30 acres in Sector 16.
places.description: Shaded paths wind through beds of many rose varieties. The Rose Festival each February draws big crowds.
places.history: Named after Zakir Husain, a former President of India.

places.name: Government Museum and Art Gallery
places.shortDescription: A Le Corbusier building in Sector 10, with Gandhara sculpture and Pahari paintings.
places.description: Fine collections of Gandhara Buddhas, Pahari miniature paintings and modern Indian art, in a concrete museum designed by Le Corbusier.

sources.title: Government Museum and Art Gallery, Chandigarh – Wikipedia

images.alt: Government Museum and Art Gallery, Chandigarh

places.name: Sukhna Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A 2,600-hectare forest in the Shivalik Hills, just behind Sukhna Lake.
places.description: A quiet forest on the northern edge of the city, with trails and watchtowers, that's home to sambar, peacocks and many birds.

places.name: Open Hand Monument
places.shortDescription: Le Corbusier's giant metal hand, the emblem of Chandigarh, in the Capitol Complex.
places.description: A 26 m metal sculpture that turns in the wind. It stands for 'open to give, open to receive'.
places.history: Part of the Capitol Complex, on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
